sols: The digit in the second decimal place is 8; the next digit is 2.
look at the third decimal place

parts.t:
By writing each number correct to 1 significant figure, estimate the value of this calculation.
You must show your working.
Use your calculator to work out the value of the calculation, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: Round each number to 1 significant figure: 58.3 → 60, 41.6 → 40, 0.492 → 0.5, 9.87 → 10.

items.stem:
A rectangular card has length 8.6 cm and width 5.3 cm.
Each measurement is correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.t: Write down the lower bound of the length.
Work out the lower bound of the perimeter of the card.

ms:
M1 for 2 × (8.55 + 5.25) or 8.55 + 8.55 + 5.25 + 5.25
A1 cao
FT their 8.55 with lower bound 5.25
sols: The length is given to 1 decimal place, so it could be up to 0.05 cm out.
The perimeter is smallest when both sides are smallest.
adding, so use both lower bounds

items.stem:
The mass of one box of tiles is 4.7 kg, correct to the nearest 0.1 kg.
A pallet holds 12 of these boxes.

parts.t: Write down the lower bound of the mass of one box.
Calculate the upper bound of the total mass of the 12 boxes.

sols: The mass is given to the nearest 0.1 kg, so the rounding unit is 0.1 kg.
subtract half of the rounding unit
The total is greatest when every box is as heavy as possible.

ms:

A1 cao
sols: Round each number to 1 significant figure: 9.68 → 10, 40.3 → 40, 0.196 → 0.2.
choose numbers that give an exact square root

items.stem:
A rectangular playing field measures 46 m by 28 m.
Each measurement is correct to the nearest metre.

parts.t: Calculate the upper bound of the area of the field.
Calculate the lower bound of the area of the field.

sols: 46 m to the nearest metre lies between 45.5 and 46.5; 28 m lies between 27.5 and 28.5.
half of the 1 m rounding unit is 0.5 m
The area is greatest when both measurements are greatest.
The area is least when both measurements are least.

items.stem:
A jug of juice has mass A = 260 g, correct to the nearest 10 g.
An empty jug has mass B = 185 g, correct to the nearest 5 g.

parts.t: Calculate the upper bound of A − B.
Calculate the lower bound of A − B.

sols: A lies between 255 and 265; B lies between 182.5 and 187.5.
For the greatest difference, take the largest A and the smallest B.
subtracting, so the bounds swap over
For the smallest difference, take the smallest A and the largest B.
the true value lies between the bounds

items.stem:
Nadia runs 400 m, correct to the nearest metre, in a time of 54.8 seconds, correct to 1 decimal place.
Her average speed is distance⁄time .

parts.t:
Calculate the upper bound of her average speed.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the lower bound of her average speed.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: Distance lies between 399.5 and 400.5 m; time lies between 54.75 and 54.85 s.
Speed is greatest when the distance is greatest and the time is least.
dividing, so the denominator bound swaps over
Speed is least when the distance is least and the time is greatest.

items.stem:
A solid metal cube has edge length 6.2 cm, correct to 1 decimal place.
The mass of the cube is 1740 g, correct to the nearest 10 g.
Density = mass⁄volume .

parts.t: Write down the upper bound of the edge length.

Calculate the lower bound of the density of the metal.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the upper bound of the density of the metal.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: The edge is given to 1 decimal place, so the rounding unit is 0.1 cm.
add half of the rounding unit
nearest 10 g, so half the unit is 5 g
Density is least when the mass is least and the volume is greatest.
Lower bound of the density = 7.11 g/cm3 (3 s.f.)
Density is greatest when the mass is greatest and the volume is least.
Upper bound of the density = 7.50 g/cm3 (3 s.f.)

parts.t:
Calculate the upper bound of y.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the lower bound of y.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Write down the value of y to an appropriate degree of accuracy.
Give a reason for your answer.

ms:
B1 for 8
B1 for a reason: both bounds round to 8 correct to 1 significant figure, so only the first figure is reliable
FT their bounds
sols: each is correct to 1 d.p., so half the unit is 0.05
y is greatest when the numerator is greatest and the denominator is least.
y is least when the numerator is least and the denominator is greatest.
Correct to 1 significant figure both bounds are 8; correct to 2 significant figures they are 7.9 and 8.1, which do not agree.
compare the bounds figure by figure
y = 8, because the upper and lower bounds agree only to 1 significant figure.
only figures common to both bounds can be relied on
